newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish electricity rates set to fall.
newsitem.headline: Spanish electricity rates set to fall.

text.p: Spanish electricity rates will fall eight percent on average in the next five years due to a new electricity protocol, Industry Minister Josep Pique said at the weekend.

The government and electric companies are expected to sign the agreement on a new framework this week though the exact time has yet to be announced. Pique presented details of the protocol at a news conference in Barcelona on Saturday.
The electricity sector will be liberalised from 1998, allowing companies to buy coal on the free market.
The protocol envisions a reduction of about three percent in electricity rates in 1997, two percent in 1988 and about one percent per year in 1999-2001.

The government acknowledged the issue of "sunk costs" in the liberalisation of the sector -- costs which the government has traditionally subsidised such as those incurred from a moratorium on nuclear power, from coal generation and investments in assets.
The companies will be allowed to pass on the costs, estimated at close to 2 trillion pesetas, via tariffs in the next 10 years.
The liberalisation of the electricity sector will also allow foreign companies to compete in Spain from 1998 and set prices freely.
